results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices 17–21% effective… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices 17–21% effective today; second price increase in three months; NBIS/IREN/CRWV gain in sync

Trade press Slicast · September 30, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: Yahoo Finance

N ebius is raising prices on its GPU compute resources effective October 1, marking the second price increase in three months as the company scales its global AI infrastructure and secures additional financing tied to deployed capacity.

The price hikes affect Nvidia's latest processors. H100 GPUs will rise 17% to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85. H200 pricing increases 20% to $5.40 from $4.50, while B200 will climb 19% to $8.50 from $7.15. The largest increase applies to the B300, with rates rising 21% to $9.50 per GPU-hour from $7.85.

CPU-only compute services also face increases. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory increases 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. The ultimate impact on customer bills depends on their specific configurations and usage patterns.

The timing reflects robust demand for AI infrastructure. In July, Nebius secured approximately $775 million in debt financing backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted customer cash flows. Last month, the company reported Q2 revenue of $582.3 million, a 454% increase year-over-year, driven by AI Cloud revenue surging 514% to $574.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $236.2 million profit from a $21 million loss a year earlier.

Management reaffirmed guidance for $3 billion to $3.4 billion in 2026 revenue and expects to achieve $7 billion to $9 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end. Morningstar analysts noted that higher GPU spot prices driving higher-priced contracts would significantly improve profitability in late 2026 and 2027.

Markets responded positively to the announcement. Nebius rallied over 6% in overnight trading Wednesday, while neocloud peers IREN Ltd. and CoreWeave gained 3–4% each. Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman wrote on X: "AI demand remains off the charts. $NBIS raising prices 20% is just another example of that demand." On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for NBIS shifted to bullish from neutral.

results.title: Huurprijs voor Europese GPU-capaciteit stijgt tot 21 procent - MSP Business
highlights:
Nebius verhoogt per 1 oktober 2026 zijn uurprijzen voor het huren van GPU-capaciteit met 17 tot 21 procent. Dat blijkt uit de maandelijkse Europese GPU-prijsindex van onderzoeksbureau Lindstead. Volgens dezelfde index huur je een NVIDIA H100 bij Europese aanbieders nog steeds voor ongeveer de helft van de prijs bij AWS en Microsoft Azure.

De prijsverhoging bij het in Amsterdam gevestigde Nebius geldt voor meerdere GPU-generaties. Een NVIDIA H100 gaat van ongeveer €3,38 naar €3,95 per uur ($3,85 naar $4,50). Voor de B300, de nieuwste generatie, stijgt het uurtarief van ongeveer €6,88 naar €8,33 ($7,85 naar $9,50).

Lindstead plaatst de verhoging in een bredere ontwikkeling. Volgens het bureau is de mediane huurprijs van een H200 in twaalf maanden met ongeveer 25 procent gestegen. Daarnaast constateert Lindstead dat elke nieuwe GPU-generatie per uur duurder is dan de vorige.

### Europese aanbieders onder hyperscalerprijzen

Uit de index blijkt dat Europese aanbieders een H100 op on-demandbasis verhuren voor ongeveer de helft van de prijs bij AWS en Microsoft Azure, en voor ongeveer een derde van het tarief bij Google Cloud. Het Franse OVHcloud rekent volgens de index ongeveer €2,62 per uur, het Finse Verda €3,09 en Nebius vanaf 1 oktober €3,95. Scaleway uit Frankrijk vermeldt prijzen vanaf €2,73 per uur.

Bij de Amerikaanse hyperscalers liggen de uurtarieven voor een H100 hoger. AWS rekent €6,03, Microsoft Azure €6,12 en Google Cloud €9,71 per uur.

Lindstead baseert de cijfers op de prijspagina’s van de aanbieders en op getdeploying.com, geraadpleegd op 27 september 2026. Dollarprijzen zijn omgerekend tegen de ECB-referentiekoers van 25 september 2026 (1 euro = 1,1403 dollar). De vergelijking betreft openbare on-demandprijzen. Tarieven bij reserveringen, langlopende contracten of maatwerkafspraken kunnen afwijken.

...

### Over de index

De Europese GPU-prijsindex vergelijkt maandelijks de openbare on-demandprijzen van Europese en Amerikaanse cloudaanbieders voor de NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 en B300. Per aanbieder vermeldt de index ook het hoofdkantoor en de eigenaar. Lindstead geeft aan geen commissies van aanbieders te ontvangen.

results.title: AWS reportedly lifts GPU capacity prices again, with a 15% hike flagged for October 7
highlights:
Amazon Web Services may be raising prices on its reserved GPU compute yet again. A post on X claims AWS is lifting reserved compute prices for a fourth quarter, with a 15% increase set to begin October 7.

## What AWS has actually raised in 2026

The increases center on EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML. That product lets customers lock in GPU capacity for machine learning workloads ahead of time.

The first confirmed move came in January 2026. AWS raised Capacity Block prices by approximately 15%, with the hike landing on instances that run NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

A second, larger bump followed on July 1, 2026. That one added roughly 20% to the same GPU capacity service.

The effect shows up clearly on a single machine. After the July change, the H200-based p5e.48xlarge instance went from about $34.61 per hour to about $39 per hour in most regions. In the US West region, the post-July price for that instance reached $49.74 per hour.

The October 7 increase is a different story. The 15% figure comes from the X post, and research findings indicate that number has not been publicly confirmed by AWS.

...

AWS has reportedly framed these changes as a response to supply and demand.

The scope of the increases is narrow on purpose. They hit reserved capacity carved out for GPU workloads, not standard on-demand instances or general Reserved Instances.

Capacity Blocks let customers book GPU capacity up to eight weeks ahead of time. The reservations can also be shared across accounts, which helps larger organizations spread capacity between teams.

results.title: Korean Neocloud Firms Race to Raise Cash for GPUs - Seoul Economic Daily
highlights:
South Korean neocloud companies are accelerating fundraising to secure graphics processing units (GPUs) and expand cloud infrastructure. As surging demand for artificial intelligence computing draws investor interest, these firms are raising their funding targets or pursuing follow-on rounds. With the proceeds going into supply chain expansion and operating technology development, competition to secure a stable GPU supply is expected to intensify.

...

These companies are focused on raising cash because the neocloud market is growing rapidly as the spread of generative AI drives explosive demand for high-performance GPUs. Neocloud firms secure GPUs in bulk, supply them to companies on demand and provide environments optimized for AI computing. Citing that competitive edge, research firm Gartner has projected that neocloud providers will account for 20% of an AI cloud market expected to be worth $267 billion in 2030. Against that backdrop, Korean firms are moving to seize the opportunity and take the lead in the business.

In Korea, too, GPU supply is failing to keep pace with demand. Some neocloud companies are finding it difficult even to accept inquiries about on-demand services, which let customers rent GPUs as needed. Supply is already tight enough to meet demand from customers seeking large-scale, long-term GPU use.

As a result, competition among neocloud companies to secure GPUs is expected to intensify. Korean firms plan to put the money they have raised into expanding GPU supply chains and into research and development on GPU interconnection and operation. VESSL AI and Mondrian AI in particular run their cloud businesses with most of their GPUs secured through contracts with outside suppliers and companies. That is why the ability to secure GPUs is seen as a key variable separating winners from losers. Mondrian AI linked up with CoreWeave and Nebius as GPU suppliers this year. VESSL AI secured more than 1,000 B200 units through SK Telecom (017670) in August.

An official in the startup sector said Korean neocloud companies have until now competed mainly on price, offering the lowest rates at about half the cost of general-purpose cloud providers. "Now what will matter is the ability to stably operate GPUs scattered across multiple locations, along with AI services," the official said.

results.title: At two major GPU clouds, renting an H100 costs more than it did in March. For a CFO weighing a GPU commitment against paying for tokens, the business case changes. | Julien SIMON
highlights:
At two major GPU clouds, renting an H100 costs more than it did in March. For a CFO weighing a GPU commitment against paying for tokens, the business case changes.

Same GPU, H100 SXM on-demand, per GPU-hour:
➡️ Runpod Secure Cloud: $2.69 (17 March) to $3.49 (27 September), up 30%
➡️ Lambda, 8-GPU node: $3.44 (16 March) to $3.99 (27 September), up 16%

What it means for a business case: a GPU rental budget priced on March rates at these two clouds now needs 16% to 30% more. If a GPU commitment is on the table, rerun the numbers first, and price every workload both ways, as tokens and as rented GPUs.

results.title: Serverless GPU from a Docker image: what the platforms run
highlights:
- A model catalogue, a container runner and a GPU VM are three products: per-token, per-second or per-minute, and per-hour billing, with different ownership.
- Lyceum's serverless GPU product runs a customer's Docker image and bills per second: L40S $1.69/hr, H100 $3.59/hr, B200 $6.29/hr (read 2026-09-22).
- Of eight European GPU platforms compared, three run a customer's container image on GPUs (two bill per second, OVHcloud AI Deploy per minute); five list VMs, dedicated servers or model serving.
- Nebius lists an HGX H100 at $3.85/GPU-hour on demand, and Scaleway a 1-GPU L4 instance at €0.79/hr before tax (pages read 22 September 2026).
- In the container route the customer keeps the runtime, the model weights and the health check; no platform page read states a GPU cold-start figure.

...

A reader who wants to hand over a container rather than manage a machine can run a Docker image on Lyceum's serverless GPU product, billed per second: L40S $1.69/hr, H100 $3.59/hr, B200 $6.29/hr (read 2026-09-22) [1]. Two other providers also run a customer image on GPUs (read 30 September 2026). OVHcloud AI Deploy deploys an application or model via Docker onto replicas within a minimum and maximum node count, fixed or adapting to the workload, and bills each node per minute: an H100 node at $3.39/hr, an L40S at $1.69/hr and an L4 at $0.91/hr, excluding VAT [2]. A Nebius Serverless AI endpoint takes a container image, runs it on a container VM with or without GPUs, serves requests until it is stopped and bills per second of usage [3]. The other five providers list GPU virtual machines, dedicated servers or model serving (read 2026-09-22), where the customer assembles scaling themselves.

results.title: AI Computing Demand Diverges: H100 Prices Drop, B200 Rebounds, DRAM Pulls Back After Five Consecutive Gains · nashnova
highlights:
## GPU rentals — why are new chips rising while old ones fall?

A100 rental average: $1.59 per GPU-hour, down 2.8% MoM. H100 average: $2.64, down 2.6% MoM. Both older models are sliding, and the declines are widening.

B200 moved the opposite way: September average rebounded to $5.70, up 1.3% MoM, reversing August's dip. The B200-to-H100 price ratio rose to 2.16×.

This means → the market still pays a premium for the latest generation of compute, but supply pressure on older GPUs is intensifying. This reflects a "generational split" — new chips in demand, old chips in surplus — rather than an across-the-board move.
